findings.suggestedSeverity: Low (borderline Medium if story 103 broadcasts on the un-rewired core before 30 Oct)
findings.codeSnippet:
sOut = ICutoverERC20(l.sUSDS).balanceOf(p.owner) - sBefore;   // L389, simulation value
...
ICutoverERC20(l.sUSDS).approve(p.uniV2Router, sAmt);            // L425, baked

    .addLiquidity(l.sUSDS, l.phUSD, sAmt, pAmt, sMin, pMin, l.newPooler, p.seedDeadline); // L429-430, baked sAmt/pAmt
findings.description: Under forge --broadcast, step 5's exit and step 6's seed are separate OWNER transactions, and step 6's desired amounts sAmt/pAmt are the step-5 balance deltas measured in SIMULATION. In PROPORTIONAL mode (the pool is live today: isPoolPaused=false), any Balancer swap mined between simulation and the step-5 exit moves the per-BPT composition. One leg then pays out less than the baked amount while still clearing the on-chain minAmountsOut floor, which _checkMinAmountsOut allows to sit up to 1% below the share. The Router02 transferFrom(owner, pair, sAmt) for the short leg then fails. The owner holds 0 spare sUSDS and only 1.47 phUSD, so any sUSDS shortfall, or any phUSD shortfall above 1.47, reverts the step-6 tx on-chain. The longer leg's surplus would in any case stay on the EOA, unseeded.
findings.attackVector: Organic: the pool saw 5 swaps in the last ~7 days. Adversarial: watch the mempool for OWNER's removeLiquidityProportional and front-run it with a dust swap in either direction. This is the same ~$0.03 trigger as ycn L-28. Here the exit SUCCEEDS (it stays inside the floors) and the seed reverts. Under a --slow Ledger broadcast forge then halts. State: ~18,572 sUSDS + ~22,559 phUSD (live share of 20,401.8 BPT) sit on the OWNER EOA, which is exactly what story 103's 2026-10-07 'no funds through any EOA' requirement forbids. UniPoolerV2 is deployed but unseeded, the canonical pair exists and is empty and public (poisonable, see 9a694ae01fe1), and index 4/hook are still on the old pooler. There is no resume entry point: re-running _runCutover fails step 5 (bptIn == 0, L374). Without --slow, steps 7-12 would still land after the failed seed and cut index 4 over to an UNSEEDED pooler.
findings.impact: Liveness and custody: protocol liquidity is stranded on an EOA until a hand-written recovery runs, and the new pair stays exposed to the 2-wei poisoning brick in the meantime. No third-party theft path. The owner controls the EOA.
findings.fix: Story 103's escrow rewire removes this: escrow.exitAndSeed is atomic and seeds whole balances, so a mid-air composition change can only revert the whole tx cleanly (ycn L-28). Until the rewire lands, the core must not be broadcast in PROPORTIONAL mode. If it is kept, seed desired = the on-chain-guaranteed floors (minAmountsOut), not the simulation deltas, and sweep the remainder in a later step.
relatedLedger: yield-claim-nft L-28 d77a482de757 (same trigger, escrow design: clean revert)

findings.description: The 'read live after step 10' amounts are read in simulation and baked into the rescue calldata. The drain checks at L532-535 and in _assertRetired run only in simulation. Until the step-10 tx is mined, index 4 still dispatches to the old pooler, and every interim mint wraps USDS into sUSDS ON the old pooler (BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch). That sUSDS is not covered by the baked rescue. It stays on the old pooler after step 12 pauses it. The mint rate since the 2026-10-01 holding pattern is ~1,957 sUSDS in ~12 days. Conditional brick: if the owner re-enables the donation on the old pooler before the cutover (live batchDonationSize is 0, so this does NOT apply to today's config), an interim mint's PSM sweep consumes the parked USDS. The on-chain balance can then fall below the baked usdsRescued, so the step-11 USDS rescue reverts. The broadcast halts before step 12, leaving the old pooler unpaused with NFTMinterV2 still its minter.
findings.attackVector: No attacker needed. Ordinary index-4 mints landing during the multi-transaction broadcast window are enough.
findings.impact: Funds are not lost: rescueERC20 is onlyOwner and NOT pause-gated (BalancerPoolerV2 L437). But the retired pooler silently keeps protocol sUSDS that the in-script post-conditions claim is zero. The story-103 verify must re-read balances live after broadcast.
findings.fix: Move the step-11 rescue after step 10 has been MINED, in a second script invocation, or have story 103's verify assert old-pooler sUSDS/USDS == 0 live and sweep any residual.

findings.codeSnippet:
ICutoverMintDebtHook(p.mintDebtHook).setDispatcher(l.newPooler);   // L449, tx N
... ~10 step-9 setter txs ...
m.replaceDispatcher(p.dispatcherIndex, l.newPooler);               // L493, tx N+~12
findings.description: After step 8's setDispatcher lands, BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.onDispatch reverts OnlyDispatcher for the old pooler (hook L109-110). ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch calls hook.onDispatch unconditionally, so every index-4 mint reverts until step 10 is mined. In between sit setHook plus the step-9 setters: setMinter, setPSM, setMaxTout, setBatchMinter, setBatchDonationSize, setAuthorizedPooler x4 and setNudgeStreamer, about 11 Ledger-signed --slow transactions. The window is inherent to three independent owner contracts. The real hazard is that the core is not resumable. If the broadcast halts anywhere in steps 8-10 (Ledger timeout, gas, nonce), index 4 stays bricked, and re-running _runCutover fails step 0 L297 (hook.dispatcher != oldPooler). Story 103 says 'resume from receipts', but the core has no skip-if-done gates to resume through.
findings.impact: Index-4 mints revert, with user transactions failing and no fund loss, for the window, and indefinitely if the run halts inside it.
findings.fix: Move step 9's configuration before step 8 (it touches only the new pooler) so steps 8-10 are three consecutive transactions. Give story 103 per-step idempotent gates (as StableStakerCutoverCore did after L-02 2c82d65e65e1), or disable index 4 in NFTMinterV2 across the window.

findings.type: mock-fidelity gap hiding a mainnet precondition
findings.description: On mainnet, a Balancer V3 pool being paused does not put it in Recovery Mode. Someone must call the permissionless Vault.enableRecoveryMode(pool) first. Live today: isPoolInRecoveryMode = false. The core's RECOVERY branch never calls it. MockBalancerVault conflates the two states (poolPaused => recovery allowed, L243), so test_cutover_recovery 'proves' a property that does not hold on mainnet. The DeployMocks rehearsal (PROPORTIONAL only) does not exercise it either. The yield-claim-nft escrow fork test does call enableRecoveryMode explicitly (UniPoolerCutoverEscrow.fork.t.sol L216).
findings.impact: Fail-closed. After 30 Oct, a RECOVERY_EXIT=true run reverts in simulation (PoolNotInRecoveryMode) unless an operator enables recovery mode first. This is liveness only, at the deadline-pressured moment.
findings.fix: In the RECOVERY branch, call vault.enableRecoveryMode(pool) when !isPoolInRecoveryMode(pool), or add it as a step-0 precondition. Make MockBalancerVault model recovery mode independently.

findings.type: cross-contract: helper enables first-LP poisoning of the cutover pair
findings.description: The helper gates liquidity on the canonical pair EXISTING, not on it having reserves. Story 111 deploys the helper BEFORE the cutover. The pair exists from cutover step 1 onward, and earlier if anyone calls the permissionless factory.createPair. Any addLiquidity through the helper while the pair is still empty makes that caller the first LP and gives the pair non-zero reserves. That permanently fails core step 2 (L339/344) and the escrow's PairNotEmpty, and UniPoolerV2's canonical-pair constructor check means no alternative pair can be used. The deploy script's NatSpec (DeployUniswapHelperMainnet.s.sol L43-46) presents 'pair does not exist' as the safety boundary. That boundary does not cover the step-1..step-6 window or a pre-created pair.
findings.attackVector: Unlike the ledgered attacker poisoning, this can be triggered by an honest user or a UI build that exposes the add-liquidity form once the pair address resolves. The helper resolves it live via getPair, independent of the PhusdSusdsPair address-book key.
findings.impact: Bricks the Balancexit cutover design (same end state as ycn L-26, which is wont-fix on the premise of an adversarial 1-wei grief). The first LP also sets the price.
findings.fix: In the helper's add functions, revert when either reserve is zero (e.g. EmptyPair), so the helper can never be the first LP. Seeding stays the cutover's job.
relatedLedger: yield-claim-nft L-26 b2a29359fde5 (wont-fix; premise was adversarial-only)

findings.description: The address and indices are correct (coins(0)=DOLA, 3pool coins(1)=USDC, so underlying index 2 = USDC). But at block 26181407 the pool holds only ~1,889 DOLA and ~1,488 3CRV. get_dy_underlying returns: 100 DOLA -> 99.62 USDC; 10,000 USDC -> 1,888.7 DOLA (-81%). Every DOLA leg crosses this pool with a 0 intermediate minimum. Only the caller's final minOut protects them.
findings.attackVector: A caller passing minOut == 0, or a UI computing minOut loosely, on a DOLA route above ~$1k loses most of the value. The helper's own quote (get_dy_underlying) reflects the loss, so a quote-derived minOut does protect the user.
findings.impact: The DOLA route is effectively unusable above small sizes. User funds are at risk only with minOut == 0.
findings.fix: Pick a deep DOLA venue before broadcasting story 111, and have the UI block or warn on DOLA quotes with price impact above a threshold.

findings.type: story-spec hazard (Law 2 / Law 1 flag) in the pending story-103 rewire
findings.description: Story 103 (incomplete, checklist L202) has step 2 DROP the skim and 'only assert the pair is empty (reserves AND balances (0,0))'. With the skim gone, a 1-wei UNSYNCED transfer to the pair fails the simulation at step 2. Yet escrow.exitAndSeed would harmlessly skim exactly that donation to newPooler (escrow L365-366). The spec turns a self-healing condition into a griefable DoS. Separately, the current core's _assertRetired (L552-553) requires owner BPT == 0. Story 103 (L203) correctly says the rewired core must NOT revert on non-zero owner BPT. That require has to be removed in the rewire, or a 1-wei BPT donation to OWNER before simulation becomes a grief.
findings.attackVector: 1 wei of sUSDS or phUSD transferred to the pair before simulation.
findings.impact: Liveness only, and marginal: an attacker can already sync, which is the 9a694ae01fe1 brick.
findings.fix: In the rewire, assert reserves == (0,0) only and leave balances to the escrow's skim. Drop the owner-BPT clause from _assertRetired.

clearedChecks.verdict: Already ledgered in yield-claim-nft: L-26 b2a29359fde5 (wont-fix), Q-24 88bfa9493621, L-27 2268ead7cba4 (fix-pending), L-28 d77a482de757 (fix-pending), F-02-052 5a7732a4ea71 (fix-pending). Not re-filed.

Cleared. abort returns BPT/sUSDS/phUSD/USDS only to the immutable oldPooler. BalancerPoolerV2.withdrawBPT/rescueERC20 are onlyOwner, any token, and NOT pause-gated, so funds stay recoverable even after step 12 pauses the old pooler. The residual is the L-27 setPool case, already ledgered.

Consistent with story 103: UniPoolerV2 (needs the pair to exist, canonical) -> escrow (reads newPooler.pair/router/sUSDS/phUSD, snapshots oldPooler.pool) -> withdrawBPT(escrow). sUSDS.asset()==primeToken and the old/new sUSDS match are checked.

A third-party donation to the escrow cannot be extracted at a profit: constant-product arbitrage recovers less than the gift. Operational note for story 103: the old pooler's 1,957.66 sUSDS must keep going straight to newPooler (core step 11), never into the escrow before exitAndSeed, or it would be seeded one-sided (+10.5% to the sUSDS leg).

The core at a4f9f3c does not reference the escrow. Every divergence (skim destination, EOA custody, floors checked on owner balance, USDS route, owner-BPT post-condition) is enumerated in story 103's rewire checklist (L202-206). The story is still incomplete, so the rewire is pending, not missed. The rewire-specific hazards are CODE-001 and CODE-007.

Cleared. Every path delivers the final output to the recipient and enforces minOut (swaps on the final amount; adds via Router02 mins; removes on both legs after the burn). Refunds: addLiquidity leftovers are returned, and the unused sUSDS on the USDS path is redeemed to USDS. The PSM buyGem floor dust is refunded as USDS to the recipient (psmGemForUsds matches the DssLitePsm cost rounding). ETH is accepted only from WETH, and the ETH send comes last, with no state left to re-enter. The helper holds zero balance after each call. minOut == 0 is caller-chosen (SEMGREP-001/002 are false positives: intermediate 0 mins sit inside one atomic tx under the final guard). MR-008: when the USDC leg floors to 0, the whole USDS goes to the recipient and ethOut = 0, which reverts unless minEthOut == 0. Dust-scale (<1e12 wei USDS) and caller-chosen.
